basis_affected_use_analysis.clause: In our positive left-over-right convention, increasing top-vertex order makes them descending: a pair that crosses once has its initially left strand still on the left just before that crossing, so that strand crosses over.
basis_affected_use_analysis.proposed: In the positive right-over-left convention, these permutation braids are descending for the auxiliary traversal in decreasing top-vertex order: a pair that crosses once has its initially right strand still on the right just before that unique crossing, so that strand crosses over and is traversed first. This auxiliary traversal is not the increasing-initial-endpoint traversal defining the standard matching basis in the Statement; the positive permutation lifts need not be those standard basis representatives. Their use below requires their braid-word identities and distinct connectors, for which step 4.1 permits arbitrary representatives.
basis_affected_use_analysis.proof_reasoning: For a reduced positive permutation braid each crossed pair crosses once. Its initially right member remains right until that crossing and goes over, so decreasing initial-position traversal meets every crossing over first. This is auxiliary, not the fixed increasing-order basis traversal. The remainder of8.3 proves positive permutation word uniqueness by braid/distant relations; shuffle length-additivity and cup-slide identities do not depend on traversal order. Steps13.1 and12.1 need distinct connectors and4.1 independence for arbitrary representatives, not equality to the standard descending representatives. Step13.2 explicitly permits arbitrary strand order; taking the largest endpoint strand above fits right-over and its positive string. Subsequent14–18 algebraic filtration/induction identities remain unchanged. No claim of a full independent mathematical audit beyond this convention impact.

assigned_convention_interfaces.quote: 3.1 Let $N$ be the number of matchings and choose the $N$ source basis elements supplied by [F5]. They define a surjection $u:T^N\to BMW_n(T)$, and step 2.1 gives the surjection $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. Identify the target with $T^N$ using step 1.1. The composite $A=\Phi_nu:T^N\to T^N$ is a surjective square matrix over the commutative ring $T$. Choose a preimage of each of its finitely many standard basis vectors to obtain $B$ with $AB=I$. Then $\det(A)\det(B)=1$, so the adjugate formula makes $A$ invertible. If $x\in\ker\Phi_n$, write $x=u(v)$; then $Av=0$, hence $v=0$ and $x=0$. Thus $\Phi_n$ is injective as well as surjective. Its inverse transports the standard matching basis to the abstract BMW algebra, proving all the stated freeness and rank assertions, including $n=0,1$. No implication from target freeness alone is used: the finite source spanning bound [F5] is essential. [F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
